scenes.headline: withColumn()
scenes.subtitle: Adding or replacing a single column.
scenes.narration: The withColumn transformation adds a new column or replaces an existing one using an expression.

scenes.headline: What withColumn does
items: Adds a new column from an expression
Replaces a column if the name already exists
Returns a new DataFrame — originals are immutable
Chains naturally for multiple derived columns
scenes.narration: WithColumn adds a new column from an expression, or replaces an existing column if the name already matches. Because DataFrames are immutable it returns a new one, and it chains naturally when you need several derived columns.

scenes.headline: Deriving new columns
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, upper

df = (transactions_df
    .withColumn("total_cost", col("item_count") * col("price_per_item"))
    .withColumn("region", upper(col("region"))))
scenes.narration: We add a total_cost column by multiplying item_count and price_per_item, then chain a second withColumn that replaces region with its uppercase form. Each call returns a fresh DataFrame, so the transformations stack cleanly.

scenes.text: Avoid hundreds of chained withColumn calls — use a single select for many columns.
scenes.narration: For many columns at once, prefer a single select over hundreds of chained withColumn calls, which can bloat the query plan.
